what_this_is: E4's committed constructed class: integer-coefficient univariate polynomials, half with a rational root and half without, frozen BEFORE the registered run scores the procedure against them.
The floor is ALL OF IT, whatever its size — the design says '100 of 100 over a class declared as >= 100 is a floor that cannot be checked'.
why_a_constructed_class_and_not_the_corp: Correction 5: the corpus reach of NIHIL is THREE statements — sqrt_two_irrational, sqrt_prime_irrational, and leanworkbook.skel.lean_workbook_49423 — and all three carry `sqrt` or `Real.sqrt`, a call head outside the evaluator, so none is compiled by this cycle's machinery.
The answer TYPE survives whole; the temptation to size it by corpus coverage does not. NO CORPUS-COVERAGE NUMBER IS QUOTED FOR NIHIL anywhere in this cycle, because the honest one is zero.
how_the_key_is_justified_independently_o: The with-root half is built by FACTORING: (qx - p)(x^2 + ax + b) has the rational root p/q by construction, before any procedure looks at it.

The without-root half rests on the rational root theorem rather than on the procedure's own output: a rational root of x^2 - n must be an integer dividing n, and an integer root would make n a perfect square. Same for cubes.
A key produced by the instrument under test would make E4 a tautology, which is what this paragraph exists to prevent.
